source.title: Deduplicating Training Data Makes Language Models Better
source.authors: Katherine Lee; Daphne Ippolito; A. Nystrom; Chiyuan Zhang; Douglas Eck; Chris Callison-Burch; Nicholas Carlini

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Reports how training/validation overlap and deduplication affect validation perplexity, but does not measure training error or test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study does not test random-label memorization, width, architecture, optimizer, batch size, dropout, sharpness, or removal of influential memorized examples. Its validation-perplexity and generated-copying findings concern related effects of duplicate training data and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study measures language-model deduplication, validation perplexity and verbatim copying, which test none of V1–V8. In particular, duplicate removal is not V8's removal of examples selected by label-memorization influence, and there is no matched random-removal comparison. Using Adafactor and a fixed batch size does not test optimizer or batch-size effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that deduplication generally preserves or improves perplexity while reducing training cost, train–test overlap and memorized generation. They acknowledge that consequences for tasks requiring memorization and possible loss of attribution were not investigated.
record.recipe_differences: Studies data deduplication and language-model perplexity or copying, rather than the listed generalization interventions and measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports different perplexity outcomes by evaluation subset (duplicates versus unique) and by deduplication method; it notes that different duplicate thresholds could change the comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: Duplicate validation subsets have lower perplexity than unique subsets: 10.11 versus 23.58 for Transformer-XL, 13.77 versus 15.73 for GROVER-Base, and 7.68 versus 9.45 for GROVER-XL.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Train–validation overlap can make language-model evaluation appear better on duplicated examples.

fits_no_version.finding: Unprompted copied-token rates fall from 1.926% to 0.189% or 0.138% at one epoch, and from 1.571% to 0.264% or 0.168% at two epochs, after deduplication.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deduplicating language-model training data can reduce verbatim copying in generated output.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 6.1 reports similar perplexity on original and unique C4 validation examples, higher perplexity on duplicated examples after deduplication, and improved external-dataset perplexity in some conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-data deduplication can preserve or improve language-model perplexity while reducing performance attributable to overlapping evaluation examples.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: No training-error results or direct train/test generalization gaps are reported. The deduplicated-versus-original perplexity comparison uses different duplicate thresholds, which the authors say could change the results. Table 5 reports no uncertainty estimates; the C4 perplexity results are figures in the supplied text without extractable numeric values.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. Figure 2/7 perplexity results were not given numeric values in the supplied text and are not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy under natural versus random labels.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout effects, including interactions with dataset size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap correlations and comparisons with other measures.
Influence-based selection of memorized labeled examples, retraining after removal, and test-accuracy comparison against equal random removal.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels apply. The obstacle is the mismatch between the tested interventions and V1–V8, rather than merely the absence of training-error measurements. Figure-only perplexity results were already declared omitted in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural versus random labels.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples and comparing test-accuracy effects with random removal.

rows.note: This is a memorized-copying measure, not a train/test error gap.
rows.check: Value matches Table 4. This result uses the one-epoch checkpoint of the two-epoch training run; copying does not measure any listed version.
